stories.summary: NATO has authorised deploying an AWACS reconnaissance aircraft to Poland after prosecutors said three Russian cruise missiles fell on its territory. The flying radar has served since the Cold War, in the Balkans, in Libya and after 11 September over US airspace.
stories.article_text_excerpt: A radar also has a horizon. While a ground-based radar can have low-flying aircraft or cruise missiles hidden from it by the Earth's curvature and the terrain, viewing from higher altitude allows it to see farther. That is why NATO lifts its radar into the air, together with the soldiers who interpret the signals, relay warnings and, when needed, direct the fighter jets waiting for deployment.According to the Polish prosecutor's office, three Russian H-101 cruise missiles crashed in Poland on 20 November. Three days later NATO confirmed that General Alexus Grynkewich, the commander of the alliance's European forces, had authorised the forward deployment of an AWACS aircraft. The fleet based in Gelsenkirchen in Germany has played an important role since 2022 in monitoring the airspace over NATO's eastern flank.What makes it more than a flying radar?AWACS is an English acronym meaning airborne early warning and control system.
